Salam Ahmadyan, 36, from Liverpool, and Rahman Salehi, 34, from Salford, were arrested in Manchester on 20th September. The two Iranian nationals were charged today, Friday 2nd October, with engaging in conduct in preparation for terrorist acts, contrary to Section 5 of the Terrorism Act 2006. It is alleged that the two men were in contact with an overseas third party who may be in Iran in relation to the alleged plot. Both men have been remanded in custody and are due to appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on Saturday, 3 October. Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans, Senior National Coordinator for Counter Terrorism Policing, said: “These are extremely serious charges and allegations, and have come about from a joint CTP investigation, working closely with our partners in the security services. This investigation has led to the disruption of what we believe to have been a plot targeting the Jewish community in Manchester. I would like to reiterate that we do not believe there to be any ongoing threat to the public in relation to this matter, but as always, we would ask that people remain vigilant and contact police with any concerns. “I’m aware that the news of this alleged plot coming during the High Holy day period has caused a great deal of concern to the Jewish community, as well as with the wider public. It also coincides with the anniversary of the devastating terrorist attack last year at Heaton Park synagogue and comes in a wider context of increasing antisemitic incidents across the UK, so we are very aware that this will likely increase what were already heightened concerns amongst the Jewish community.

candidates.source_summary: Aldi, Morrisons, and Tesco have been told to ‘get their act together’ by a litter picking group who keep having to haul supermarket trolleys out of a canal.
candidates.source_title: Supermarkets criticised after trolleys end up in canal
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Aldi, Morrisons, and Tesco have been told to ‘get their act together’ by a litter picking group who keep having to haul supermarket trolleys out of a canal. Along a stretch of the Rochdale canal in Failsworth, litter picking group Clean Up Failsworth Canal said they regularly have to drag trolleys out of the water as part of their impressive efforts to clean up the area. The group, which has been running for over 13 years, goes out once a month. Armed with litter pickers and dozens of bags, the team regularly find flytipped rubbish, drinks cans, and nitrous oxide or ‘laughing gas’ cannisters. On September 20, around 22 bags of rubbish had been filled and 26 cannisters were collected while 17 trolleys were fished out of the canal. The trolleys, according to the group, are increasingly becoming a problem. In some areas such as under the bridge to the town’s Tesco car park, the dumped trolleys could even mean boats struggle to get through. Sandra Ball, who represents Failsworth West for Reform UK, said: “Tesco, Aldi, and Morrisons the other end need to get their act together and get it sorted. The trolleys have always been a problem. We have taken 20 out in one session.” She added: “At the end of the day, that cost comes back to us. They have got to pay for [new] trolleys.” Coun Ball has been involved with the group for years. Supported by Oldham council and the Canal and River Trust, she said around 90 people involved in her Failsworth litter busting team. Despite the efforts, she and others feel like it’s a ‘disheartening’ uphill battle, adding: “Within 10 minutes, someone else will have dropped something but if you do not keep on top of it, what would it look like?”

candidates.source_summary: A major plan is being developed that could power thousands of homes with the heat from baked beans, sewage, and data centres.
candidates.source_title: Homes powered by Baked Beans could be part of Greater Manchester’s future
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A major plan is being developed that could power thousands of homes with the heat from baked beans, sewage, and data centres. EnergiRaven, a UK-based green energy transition consultancy, is pitching to council bosses to introduce a network of pipes across the region. These would take captured heat from different sources and transport it to people’s homes potentially cutting down on people’s energy bills by up to 38 per cent. Nicknamed the ‘Bee Network for Heat’, the project could link homes across all ten boroughs in Greater Manchester providing heat to thousands. It is based of a publicly-owned model that has been running in Denmark for decades. A map of the network suggests sources of the heat could come from the Baked Beans factory in Wigan, a bread factory near Bolton, various data centres, a number of different industries, wastewater and sewage treatment works, and the Carrington Power Plant. Another map also suggested Kellogg’s plant near Stretford, heat from mine water near Oldham, and Asda’s distribution centre in Rochdale. At an event on September 30, the we heard a data centre in Heywood could heat the equivalent of 50,000 homes. According to EnergiRaven, enough heat could exist across the region to cover 85% of the regions needs and cut down on household bills by 38%. Over 20 years, they say a heat network could save £8.83bn. At the moment, EnergiRaven say heating costs are currently around 8.7p/kWh but this could fall to 5.4p. While gas heating costs in the UK shot up by £1273, it only rose by £271 in Denmark where homes are part of a district heating network. Those behind the scheme say it will protect homes from energy shocks caused by the wars in Iran and Ukraine by tapping into a UK-energy source. Though the scheme will come at a cost, the UK spent £39.3 billion between October 2022 and March 2023 to subsidise energy costs.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Transport in Heywood and Middleton was among the priorities for the towns brought up at the Labour Party Conference. The conference, which concluded in Liverpool on Wednesday, was the party’s first under new leader Andy Burnham. Elsie Blundell, MP for Heywood and Middleton North, said the event has seen new announcements for long overdue leasehold reform, help for first-time buyers, changes to the water system and plans to bring down energy bills. The conference also gave MPs an opportunity to meet with Government Ministers and push for important investments in their areas, including an express bus to Manchester city centre. Mrs Blundell met with the Minister for Buses and Transport, Simon Lightwood MP, to highlight the importance of an express bus link between Heywood and Manchester. She said: “It has been a vibrant and energetic Labour Party conference, on the main stage and in the policy discussions on the fringe. “The overriding sense is that we have hope again, with ideas and pledges to tackle some of our country’s biggest challenges.” READ MORE: Seven arrested during cannabis farm raids

candidates.source_summary: DCFC - Derby County sanctioned a loan move to Rochdale for Dajaune Brown in the summer, and he's back amongst the goals.
candidates.source_title: 'Beautiful': Derby County prospect rediscovering dangerous best in League Two after challenging 2025/26 season News: The72 - Football League News
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Derby County boast a strong academy, although the progression of youth players to the first-team has slowed somewhat in recent years. Among the DCFC alumni of recent seasons are Jayden Bogle, Jason Knight , Morgan Whittaker, Liam Delap and more. The Rams are still producing bright prospects though, and a handful are currently out on loan. Owen Eames has made a good impression at Falkirk having emerged in the senior picture under John Eustace last season. One prospect who started sniffing around the first-team in 2024/25 was Dajaune Brown. And, after a challenging time last season, the striker is finding form in his latest loan away from Pride Park. Nottingham-born Brown made a name for himself in Derby County ’s U18s and U21s, with prolific goalscoring prompting calls for his increased first-team involvement. After a handful of appearances for the Rams, he starred on loan in the National League with Gateshead, where he managed nine goals and eight assists in 22 games. However, injury ended his 2024/25 season early having found a place in the DCFC first-team. He then spent last term on loan at Port Vale , where he managed only three goals and three assists in 34 games as they were relegated from League One. A new loan opportunity came knocking in the summer though, with Rochdale bringing Brown in . He has swiftly found a starting role, and after six goalless games to start, the 20-year-old has found form. Brown was on the scoresheet as the Dale won 2-0 against Oldham Athletic , and he followed that up by scoring one and setting up the other in the 2-1 triumph over Fleetwood Town last weekend. His goal was praised by manager Watson post-game , who said this on Brown: “Yes, beautiful goal. That’s two and two for him. So, [the goals] gives him a lot of confidence.”

candidates.source_title: Ex-Swindon player to miss reunion as Rochdale without multiple key men - Wilts and Gloucestershire Standard
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale are dealing with a large number of injuries, including to former Swindon Town man Ryan East, ahead of their meeting this weekend. Since winning the National League playoffs and stepping up to League Two, life has been more difficult for Rochdale. They lost all of their first three matches, but have picked up of late, winning their last two and beginning an upturn under new manager Ian Watson. But they have been dealing with a number of injuries as they have managed this, with six regular first team players missing the 2-1 win at Fleetwood Town last week. This has included captain Ethan Ebanks-Landell and his likely centre-back partner Laurence Maguire. East, who was a key cog to their passing style in midfield as they won over 100 points last season, has broken his toe and will miss coming up against Town, having made 23 appearances for the club under Ben Garner. Whilst East will not be involved, Swindon will be coming up against a familiar face in Aden Flint, with whom Rochdale have taken seven points from a possible nine since he arrived. Beyond them, the impressive right-back Dan Moss is also out with an injury, as are Will Jenkins, who followed Watson from South Shields, and Casey Pettit, which means that three potential midfield options are missing.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Police have issued an update after two boys were rushed to hospital following a crash in Middleton . Emergency services descended on Windermere Road, at the junction with Wood Street, at 8pm on Monday evening (September 28). It followed a crash involving an electric bike and a car. Police and paramedics were seen in attendance following the crash while a cordon was put in place. Two boys, aged 13 and 14, suffered serious injuries following the collision. The pair were taken to hospital for treatment. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter The driver of the car, a man in his 20s, was arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by driving without due care and attention. In an update issued this morning (Friday), Greater Manchester Police said he had since been bailed pending further enquiries. The road was closed off for several hours on Monday night as investigations were carried out at the scene. Images showed evidence markers placed on the road within the cordon. GMP's Serious Collision Investigation Unit has urged anyone with information, or any witnesses of the crash. Officers also want to speak to anyone who has footage from the scene. Details can be passed on to police by calling 101 or using the LiveChat function on GMP's website, quoting log number 3478 of September 28, 2026. Alternatively, contact Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111.

candidates.source_summary: Tramservices have resumed on the Oldham-Rochdale line after essential track replacement work was successfully completed
candidates.source_title: Oldham to Rochdale Tram Line - Premier Rail
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Tramservices have resumed on the Oldham-Rochdale line after essential track replacement work was successfully completed, marking a major milestone in this summer’s programme of network improvements. The work, which took place over a planned two-week closure between Victoria and Rochdale town centre, is part of a wider £150m investment to maintain and improve Greater Manchester’s tram network. It will help deliver a smoother, more reliable service for passengers and support the long-term resilience of the network. Engineers worked day and night between Monsall and Newton Heath & Moston to replace 1.2km of track, improve drainage, renew foundations and correct the alignment and level of the track. It was a big and complex job, using around 290 new concrete sleepers, 2,000 tonnes of gravel and replacing more than 5,000 tonnes of ballast. As a result, sections of the route that previously required speed restrictions can now return to normal operation – up to 50mph on some sections – helping to improve journey times for customers. Ian Davies, TfGM’s Network Director for Metrolink, said: “This was a large and complex piece of engineering, that will make a real difference to the reliability and long-term condition of the network. “It’s the first major milestone of a wider programme of improvements we’re delivering across our tram network this summer to keep it safe, resilient and fit for the future. “We know closing a line is disruptive, and we’re very grateful for everyone continuing to bear with us while this essential work is completed.” Further improvement work will take place at other locations across the Bee Network over the coming months. The most significant being at Trafford Bar and Deansgate-Castlefield. While this work is carried out, there will be no trams on the Eccles, Trafford Centre or Altrincham lines for three weeks from Monday 13 th July to Sunday 2 nd August. Before that, further tram improvement work took place in the city centre . Further work to finish off the job on the Oldham-Rochdale line also took place on Sunday 7 th June and Sunday 12 th July. Further information on tram improvement works can be found here: https://tfgm.com/tram-improvement-works

candidates.source_summary: Renovating Rochdale's iconic Seven Sisters tower blocks would force residents out of their homes for more than a decade, housing chiefs have said.
candidates.source_title: No decision yet on College Bank – but ‘renovation would take more than a decade’ - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Renovating Rochdale’s iconic Seven Sisters tower blocks would force residents out of their homes for more than a decade, housing chiefs have said. While Rochdale Boroughwide Housing says no decision on the future of the landmark College Bank blocks has been taken, residents have asked new Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig to back their campaign to refurbish their homes rather than demolish them. But if campaigners get their wish, the scale of bringing the 61-year-old buildings up to modern standards would take more than 10 years and they could not be occupied until the work is complete, RBH chiefs have said. Members of Greater Manchester Tenants Union recently met Ms Craig to discuss the steps that could be taken to renovate almost 1,000 homes in College Bank and Lower Falinge. Plans to demolish College Bank were first discussed in 2017 when RBH warned that the buildings were approaching the end of their life. candidates.source_title: Letter to the editor from a Hopwood Hall volunteer on High Court ruling and restoration hopes
candidates.source_body_excerpt: In regards to the Hopwood Hall Estate Court Case here is my statement as a long standing volunteer. In regards to the Hopwood Hall Estate Court Case here is my statement as a long standing volunteer. I am deeply disappointed and upset by the outcome of the High Court proceedings concerning Hopwood Hall. Having been connected with the Hall for more than two decades, and having actively supported Hopwood DePree and the restoration project since 2013, this is not simply a building or a court case to me. Hopwood Hall has been an important part of my life for many years. My connection with Hopwood Hall actually began around 2003, long before the current restoration project existed. I stumbled across the Hall while walking through the surrounding woods. At that time, as I remember it, there was no fencing immediately around the Hall and I would sometimes sit on the maintained lawn outside. The building was boarded up, but even then it struck me as a hidden gem. There was something about the place that stayed with me. Around 2013, my brother and I became aware that Hopwood DePree had come forward with an interest in saving and restoring his ancestral home. We reached out to him and subsequently met him for the first time at Touchstones in Rochdale, where we went through historical archive material we had found relating to Hopwood Hall. From there, we stayed with the project. My brother and I were involved during its earliest stages and served on the original committee before the official charity was formed. When the project developed and the wider volunteer programme followed, we continued our involvement as volunteers. We were never afraid of getting our hands dirty. We helped with the gardens and grounds, supported restoration activities and assisted at open days, including undertaking security and public-facing duties. Over the years, our voluntary contribution was recognised through a number of awards, something of which we remain extremely proud. For many visitors arriving at Hopwood Hall, my brother and I were among the first people they would meet. We tried to make everyone feel welcome and to represent the project positively. We got to know many people from Middleton and the surrounding community, saw familiar faces returning to open days and had countless conversations with people who cared deeply about the future of the Hall.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Swindon Town look like they are going to be without 14 players due to injury at Rochdale, as another three players have been lost this week. After finally naming an unchanged line-up for the first time this season against Accrington Stanley, the injury bug has struck Town again, and with a vengeance. Paul Glatzel and Ollie Clarke, who both started that game, will not be involved at the Crown Oil Arena this weekend, and Matty Virtue will also drop out of the squad. Louis Millard will be back involved, although in a limited capacity, as he was initially recommended to feature for the under-18s this weekend. There had been hope that Joe Snowdon would be available for this match, but he will also not make it back in time, and that leaves Ian Holloway with quite the conundrum. All of this is in addition to the absences of Mitch Clark, who is serving the final game of his suspension, and Sam Inwood, who is on international duty with the Northern Ireland Under-21s. The squad that goes up to Greater Manchester will likely feature two goalkeepers, four centre-backs, two left-backs, two central midfielders, a winger, and two strikers. Freddie Hoare is among the under-18 players in contention to be part of the squad, as otherwise Town would be well down on numbers.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Hopwood Hall dates back to the 1400s. Credit: via Phil Longley American actor Hopwood DePree lost his court battle with the council, where he argued that the local authority had acted illegally over refusing to sell him the historic property. Dupree claims ancestral links to the grade two-listed Hopwood Hall in Middleton. Since 2017 he has worked to repair the building, documenting his efforts on YouTube and through the book Downton Shabby: One American’s Ultimate DIY Adventure. When he became involved in 2017, DePree signed an exclusivity agreement with Rochdale Council that would allow him to acquire Hopwood Hall for £1. As per the terms of the agreement, in order to do this he would have to prove the ability to refurbish the entirety of the 1400s hall. This, the council argued, had not been done – despite DePree and his group of volunteers having a successful change of use application in 2022 to turn the part of the hall into a wedding and hospitality venue. This, the council argued to the court, only represented a promise to refurbish part of the hall, not the entirety. In 2024, the council did not renew the exclusivity agreement, noting that an independent financial consultant had assessed DePree’s proposed business model for the site. The consultant said that the scheme would be loss-making and unable to secure additional funding.

In a nearby car park, a woman is getting dressed in a full-body fox get-up out of the back of a van. A man is belting anti-Brexit remixes of old pop songs through a megaphone at eight in the morning. These are just some of the sights that greeted attendees of the Labour Party Conference on their way into the Liverpool Experience Campus. Just as prominent as the frenetic energy of the conference itself – with attendees racing between venues and elbowing into the back of overflowing meeting rooms that quickly begin to smell like high school gyms – is the potpourri of protests happening outside it. Some of these have already had high-profile news coverage. On Sunday, Merseyside police arrested 82 protestors holding ‘I oppose genocide. I support Palestine Action’ signs “on suspicion of wearing/carrying an article supporting a proscribed organisation”. Detainees included 94-year-old human rights barrister Margaret Owen and Massive Attack’s singer Robert Del Naja. The arrests were criticised by Amnesty International as ‘a shameful attack on freedom of speech’. Monday saw a smaller but enduring showing of Palestine protestors at the tail end of the security queue. They did not appear to hold any signs related to Palestine Action. “We’re not going away. We’re here to send Andy Burnham a message,” said one of the activists. “The government might be making some of the right noises, but the fact is, the British government is still making us complicit. Burnham needs to act now.” At the foot of the Wheel of Liverpool, a persistent anti-Brexit campaigner has set up shop with a powerful pair of speakers, and lungs: Steve Bray. The blue-and-white-star clad character decamped from his usual position outside Westminster to treat sore-headed attendees to his EU-flavoured covers of ‘I will walk 500 miles (to rejoin the EU)’ and ‘You’ll Never Walk Alone’ – along with the European anthem. “Andy Burnham is going to kick open those doors to rejoin the EU,” Bray tells the LDRS with confidence. “His hands are currently tied by the manifesto. But he has a few years to get the message out to people, and I’m sure it will play a big role at the next election.” Mr Burnham is predicted to lay out plans to ‘edge the UK closer to the EU’ in his speech today, though he has previously said he ‘respects the decision made at the referendum’.

candidates.source_summary: Andy Burnham has delivered his speech to the Labour Party Conference, but did he do what most leaders do when their Party is facing a resurgence in the polls and could gain a new mandate to govern, if the polls are to be believed? Not really
candidates.source_title: Analysis: Did Andy Burnham's Speech bring anything new?
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Andy Burnham has delivered his speech to the Labour Party Conference, but did he do what most leaders do when their Party is facing a resurgence in the polls and could gain a new mandate to govern, if the polls are to be believed? Not really Burnham's speech focused on some main points: Triple Lock Reform, the Care System, and Energy. However, a lot of his speech was stuff we have already heard before from the Prime Minister: National Care Service, power to every UK postcode, and water - all things that Burnham either ran on or introduced following his election as Party Leader. But what does it all mean, and how will it affect you? National Care Service & Triple Lock Reform The big takeaway from this speech was the promise of the National Care Service, which centres on a care service that is free at the point of service, rather than the current Social Care provision. This means many families fork out hundreds, or even thousands, of pounds for private or council-supported care for their older relatives, and often complain about poor-quality services and poor working conditions. Burnham apologised for this, saying to the conference hall: "you are not invisible to me". He called the National Care Service essential to protecting the future of the NHS, becoming frustrated for Doctors and Nurses as he said, "we have let you down too...at risk of burnout...corridor care, your daily experience" We found out a little more about how he will fund this, with growing concerns over the last few days about a potential scrapping of the Triple Lock on State Pensions. Burnham tried to calm the waters, saying he would follow the manifesto commitment but would seek changes to the Triple Lock in 2030 by ensuring pensions rise by 2.5% while also not losing value against average earnings. This essentially downgrades the Triple Lock to a Double Lock, similar to a system that is used in Australia. However, the IFS has already said this alone would not pay for a National Care Service, which Burnham may not want to hear, as he pledged the scheme will be fully funded and won't need any additional borrowing. He also promised during his speech that Low-income Pensioners (pensioners who only have the state pension, or the state pension with a small private pension on top) will not pay tax in this Parliament. Burnham did not clarify where the limit was for those with a private pension, but the decision will largely be welcomed by those who fear the triple-lock increases will push them over the tax threshold.

candidates.source_title: Samy Kibula to bring vital experience to Rochdale Hornets - Total Rugby League
candidates.source_body_excerpt: ROCHDALE HORNETS coach Gary Thornton says Samy Kibula will provide not only the size and physical presence expected of a prop, but also a helpful amount of skill. The 27-year-old former Super League player who started out at Wigan Warriors has joined from Swinton Lions to become Hornets’ fifth close-season addition. Halfback Ben White from Batley Bulldogs is a high-profile recruit, while Rochdale aim to bring out the potential in threequarters Harry Ratcliffe (from Wakefield Trinity), Dylan Proud (Keighley Cougars) and Jack Twigg (Huddersfield Giants). Kibula, born in the Democratic Republic of the Congo before a family move to the UK, came through the Wigan system to make one appearance for the first team (in 2018). He has also played in the top flight for Warrington Wolves and Castleford Tigers, and outside it for Bradford Bulls and Batley (in two spells) as well as Swinton, where he spent this year, featuring 13 times. The 27-year-old has also had various loan stints, taking his total number of games to three figures, and having lost prop Jordan Andrade to retirement, Thornton will welcome that experience to his front row. “We are really pleased to have signed Samy, and I’d like to thank (chairman) Andy Mazey for getting this one over the line,” he said. “With Jordan not around, we needed to bring in an experienced middle-unit player, and Samy has a wealth of experience in the Championship and Super League which will be invaluable to our group.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Community equipment services provider Medequip has been awarded the contract to deliver the Community Equipment Loan Service (CELS) for Oldham, Rochdale, Stockport and Tameside (ORST). The contract has been awarded by a partnership of four local authorities, comprising Oldham, Rochdale, Stockport and Tameside councils, together with the NHS Greater Manchester Integrated Care Board (ICB). Commencing on 1 October 2026, the contract will initially run for three years, with the option to extend for up to a further two years. The service plays a vital role in supporting adults and children to live independently and safely at home. Working closely with health and social care prescribers across the four boroughs, Medequip will provide the full lifecycle management of community equipment, including procurement, delivery, installation, maintenance, repair, collection, decontamination, refurbishment and recycling. Community equipment services are a key part of integrated health and social care systems, helping to facilitate timely hospital discharge, support reablement and recovery, prevent avoidable hospital admissions and enable people to remain independent in their own homes and communities for longer. As part of the mobilisation of the new contract, Medequip will initially operate from the existing service depot in Dukinfield, ensuring continuity of service for residents and prescribing professionals. Medequip will then relocate to a purpose-built, spacious 32,450 square feet service centre depot within the Hollinwood Junction development. The modern, energy-efficient building has been designed with sustainability in mind and benefits from excellent transport and motorway connections, supporting efficient service delivery across all four boroughs. The new location will provide enhanced operational capacity and support Medequip’s continued focus on delivering responsive, high-quality services while maximising the collection, refurbishment and reuse of equipment through sustainable circular economy principles.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Luqmaan Ahmed (15/11/2001), of Heald Place, Rusholme, appeared at Manchester Crown Court earlier today, Monday 28 September 2026, and was sentenced for Encouragement of Terrorism contrary to Section 1 TACT 2006. Ahmed was sentenced to three and a half years in prison, with a one-year extended licence period. On release he will be the subject of a Serious Crime Prevention Order and part IV notification requirements under the Terrorism Act for ten years. In December 2022 Luqmaan Ahmed was sentenced to a 24-month Community Order having been convicted previously of encouraging terrorism and the dissemination of terrorist publications. He had originally been arrested in 2018 when aged 16 years old for encouraging others to join and fight for Hay’at Tahrir Al-Sham, a proscribed organisation affiliated to Al Qaida and for disseminating numerous pro-jihadist training videos via his Instagram and WhatsApp accounts. However, following conviction, but whilst awaiting sentencing, Ahmed began to post pro-Islamic State material on Instagram to a private group of Followers. On Tuesday 10 October 2023, Ahmed, then aged 21, was arrested by Counter Terrorism Policing Northwest supported by Greater Manchester Police, at his address in Rusholme for 3 counts of Section 1 Terrorism Act 2006 offences, relating to the encouragement of terrorism on social media accounts. Following a two-week trial at Manchester’s Crown Court, on Thursday 30 July 2026, the jury returned a unanimous verdict of guilty on all counts. Det Chief Supt Jonathan Chadwick, Head of Counter Terrorism Policing Northwest, said: "People posting this type of material can bring fear and distrust among our communities. “Today’s sentencing reaffirms Counter Terrorism Policing’s commitment to making sure that those who pose a risk to our society will be pursued and prosecuted. Our dedicated officers and staff, through extensive investigation have once again ensured that Luqmaan Ahmed has been brought to justice and is now facing over three years in prison. “We would encourage anyone with any concerns around people expressing extremist views, including online, to call the UK Anti-Terrorism Hotline in confidence on 0800 789 321, or alternatively, use the secure online form at gov.uk/ACT . If you see or hear something that doesn’t feel right, trust your instincts and ACT.
